newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asia dominates flow of funds to emerging countries.
newsitem.headline: Asia dominates flow of funds to emerging countries.

text.p: Asia continues to account for the lion's share of money flowing to developing countries with international capital market loans to the region hitting record levels last year, the Asian Development Bank said on Thursday.
"Seeking to develop long-term relationships with Asian corporations, the international banks made more loans to Asia than in any other region," the Manila-based bank said in its annual report.
Two of the biggest borrowers were South Korea and Thailand, accounting for about half of the total last year.

According to the Bank of International Settlements (BIS), the pace of such new lending to Asia accelerated in the first half of 1996 to reach $34.7 billion, the report said. It did not give full-year or comparative figures.
The size and dynamism of the developing Asian region have also made it increasingly important for multinational companies to have a presence.
The bank noted that companies from the European Union which had neglected the region in the 1980s were increasing their commitment through large-scale projects.
East, Southeast and South Asia attracted some $65 billion of total foreign direct investment (FDI) in 1995, up 21 percent over the previous year.
"Together they accounted for 65 percent of total developing country FDI inflows," it added.
